stem.en: Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\ s^{-2}}$. A sack of mass 5 kg rests on the floor and is lifted slowly, at constant speed, until it stands 1 m above the floor. How much work is done in lifting it? Give the answer in joules.

explanation.en: Lifting at constant speed means the upward force equals the weight, F = mg = 5 x 10 = 50 N. The sack is displaced 1 m upward, along that force, so W = F x s = 50 N x 1 m = 50 J.

hints.en: Constant speed means zero acceleration, so the upward force must exactly balance the weight.
